As you work through your emotions and memories step by step and slowly release the pressure inside, you may find yourself becoming stronger and more fulfilled.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try writing letters, and I’ll also consider seeking help from a counselor. I hope I can gradually release the emotions inside and become stronger.

I’m glad I could offer you some help. Trust in your own ability, and bravely face the emotions and challenges within you. May your journey bring healing and growth to your heart. I wish you a happy life and a happy future!

I hate him so much, but I still can’t help contacting him. Should I get divorced? My husband and I were classmates in high school. We’ve known each other for more than ten years. When we were dating as students, I felt like he could tolerate my bad temper endlessly. If I hit him or cursed at him, he could accept it, so I mistakenly thought he had a really good temper. During the two years we lived together before getting married, he also hit me twice. One time, he came home late after drinking, and I got angry. I hit him first, slapped him, and he got furious and slapped me back. The second time, I was in a bad mood and picked a fight. In front of our friends, he hit me again. But we still got married. When I was doing postpartum confinement, I was annoyed that he didn’t do anything, so I kicked him, and he slapped me in front of my mom. The day before yesterday, because he came home late and is always lying to me, and my parents were helping me take care of the child, I was afraid of waking my parents up, so I told him not to pull me back to our room to sleep. I wanted to sleep with the child. He wouldn’t listen, so I called his mother, and he got furious. He kicked the door like crazy. After my parents came out, somehow he and my dad started fighting. My dad was in the hospital for two months this year and is still recovering. We called the police, but no case was filed. He was held overnight and then released, and he didn’t come home either. I hate him so much, but I still can’t help contacting him. I really need someone to comfort me, to hold me.
I can sense how exhausted and overwhelmed you feel, carrying both hatred and a longing to see some hope beyond this confusion. What happened must have many factors behind it.
But all these years, he has always hit me. I’m really scared of him. I don’t know what to do to get away from this fear.

Yes, what you’re feeling is very understandable. When it comes to violence, we cannot tolerate or enable it; we need to respond decisively. The first priority is your safety. For your own sake and your child’s, please consider temporarily leaving him to protect your physical and emotional well-being.
But I’ve always treated him as someone I rely on. If I leave him, I’ll feel very lonely and helpless.

I understand how you feel. Leaving a relationship that has been through so much can indeed make someone feel lonely and helpless. But for your future and your child’s future, and to get away from violence, you need to bravely choose to leave. Only then can you have a better quality of life and a greater sense of happiness. And you are not alone or helpless. I’m here to support you and stay with you through this difficult time.
Really? I feel like I’ve been carrying too much pressure and too much hurt all along. Supporter, can you give me some advice?

Of course. First, you can seek help from a marriage counselor, talk about your confusion and pain, and work on the problem from a professional perspective. Second, you can spend time with relatives and friends, share your feelings, and receive more understanding and support. Most importantly, please remember to protect yourself and don’t continue to endure more harm.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll think it over carefully. Right now, I’ve decided to leave him, for my happiness and my child’s.

That is a very right decision. I’m proud of your courage and determination. By leaving him, you will have a brand-new beginning, full of hope and happiness. I will always support you. If you need any help, please tell me anytime.
Thank you for your support and encouragement. I’ll work hard to get out from under this shadow and start my life again. With your company and encouragement, I believe I can definitely do it.

Dear, you can definitely do it. No matter what difficulties and challenges you face, you can face them bravely, because you have already shown your strong and courageous side. I will always be by your side and accompany you through this difficult time.

I hate him so much, but I can’t help contacting him. Should I get divorced? My husband and I were high school classmates, and we’ve known each other for more than ten years. When we were dating as students, I felt like he could tolerate my bad temper without limit. If I hit him or yelled at him, he could accept it, so I mistakenly thought he had a really good temper.

You feel very insecure, and you hope to prove that he loves you by winning with your husband. Clearly, before marriage, you were half-believing, half-doubting his accommodation of you, so you found reasons for him before getting married. Now you hope to use legitimate reasons like the child and the elderly to win his continued tolerance, but clearly it hasn’t reached the state you hoped for.
Yes, I’ve always hoped he could change for me, but every time we argue, he always hits me. I really can’t take it.

Even though you yourself feel that sometimes you’re picking a fight, you may really not be aware that there is a willful child inside you, hoping someone will meet your needs unconditionally. And that willful child is called emotion. It always comes up for no clear reason, and you feel your husband should give way to you because you’ve given everything to him.
I understand. Maybe I’ve always expected him to care about me unconditionally, and I’ve forced my emotions onto him. But why does he always hit me?

If both of you understood a bit of basic psychology, you would say, “Honey, I’m feeling really bad today.” And if your husband happened to understand too, he would say, “Tell me about it. What kind of bad?” It’s like both of you are children, both hoping the other person will care unconditionally. Once one person sends a signal that they need care, the other shows that they need it even more.
But between us, we don’t have that kind of mechanism for mutual understanding and support. We’re always complaining that the other person isn’t good enough.

It’s also like on a cold rainy day, both people are wearing only a thin shirt, and both hope the other person will take theirs off and put it on them... If love is a fountain, it has to be supplied by an endless source of groundwater. But the two of you are like two dried-up seedling fields, refusing to give way to each other in the fight for love.
What should we do now? I’m really lost.

A person’s sense of abundance comes from three levels: the body, emotions, and the soul. For most of us, the body receives some degree of care, but emotional nourishment is much harder to be sure of, so we often feel that even when we don’t have to worry about food or clothing, we still don’t feel happy. And some people repair emotional trauma through the pursuit of a higher spiritual state.
I understand. I need to learn to express my emotional needs better, and the two of us need to look together for ways to get through this difficult situation. Thank you for your advice and support.
You’re welcome. I believe you can work through these problems. Remember, communication and understanding are the foundation of a healthy relationship. I wish you both happiness!

I hate him so much, but I still can’t stop contacting him. Should I get divorced? My husband and I were high school classmates, and we’ve known each other for more than ten years. When we were dating as students, I felt like he could tolerate my bad temper endlessly. Even if I hit him or cursed at him, he could accept it, so I mistakenly thought he had a really good temper. During the two years we lived together before getting married, he also hit me twice.

Dear, first of all, I’m sending you a big hug (づ●─●)づ. Having the courage to face your own issues already means you’re halfway there. As women, we all want a partner who loves us, cares for us, and spoils us. You’re no exception. The way you and your husband interacted back in middle school made you into a proud princess. You believed that his unlimited tolerance of your acting spoiled and being unreasonable was love.
Yes, but now I really can’t stand him anymore. He keeps bullying me, hitting me, and even argues and makes a scene with me in front of my parents. I’m in so much pain, and I don’t know what to do.
I understand your pain. Don’t think too much about what he will do. When we make decisions, we’re really doing it for ourselves. I want to know what you truly want deep down.
I want to live freely, not be controlled by him. But I also feel like I still can’t let go of all these years of feelings, and I’m worried I’ll regret it after getting divorced.

I understand. It’s very normal for you to have these thoughts. But you can’t endure pain for your whole life. Maybe we can look at it from another angle: it’s not giving up the feelings from all these years, but giving up this painful relationship. Perhaps you can sit down with him and have a good talk, and untangle what’s been weighing on both of you.
I’m afraid that if I face him, my emotions will get stirred up again, and I don’t know whether I’ll be persuaded by him.

Don’t be afraid. You’re not alone. In this moment, you’re doing the right thing. Face your pain directly, and make your thoughts clear to him. Remember, you are an independent woman, and you don’t need his agreement to make a decision.
Right, I am an independent woman. I need autonomy. But if I decide to divorce him, what will the relatives and friends around me think of me?

When your family and friends hear your story, they will understand and support whatever decision you make. What they care about is your happiness and health, not the relationship between the two of you. Also, divorce does not mean you have failed; it is a choice. You will become stronger and more independent because of it.
Thank you. I have some thoughts now, and I’ll think carefully about what I want.

You’re welcome. You can come to me anytime if you want to talk. For everyone, the path of growth is full of bumps and difficulties, but I believe you will definitely find happiness that belongs to you. Hang in there!

I hate him so much, but I still can’t help contacting him. Should I get a divorce? My husband and I were high school classmates, and we’ve known each other for more than ten years. When we were dating as students, I felt like he could tolerate my bad temper endlessly. Even if I hit him or yelled at him, he could accept it, so I mistakenly thought he had a really good temper.

I understand how you feel. Right now, you hate him and yet you can’t help contacting him, which shows that you still have feelings for him. But violence in a marriage is not something that should be tolerated; it harms both your body and your mind. Your feelings also need to be respected and cared for. You once thought he could tolerate your bad temper, but that doesn’t mean you can vent your emotions however you want. Mutual respect is a key foundation in marriage.

Yes. Before we got married, he hit me twice. I always felt it was my fault, that I had made him angry and that’s why I got hit. But now I really hate him, and I can’t forgive his violence. But I’m also afraid I’ll be very lonely without him.

Your reaction is very normal. Violence causes a lot of harm to a marriage. Hate and love both have great power, but we need to choose how to deal with these emotions. Getting along as a couple needs to be built on mutual respect and care, and you also need to protect your own physical and mental health. Although divorce may make you feel lonely, true happiness can only be felt in a healthy, equal relationship.
I know what you’re saying is right, and I also understand that only by ending this harm can I find happiness again. But I still can’t help wanting to contact him. What should I do?

What you’re feeling is very normal. After a separation, there can be emotional ups and downs. I suggest you seek more support during this process. You can talk to family and friends and look for their understanding and help. At the same time, try to develop some interests and hobbies of your own, so your life becomes richer and more varied, and gradually reduce contact with him. Remember, you are not alone; there are many people who are willing to reach out when you’re going through a difficult time.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll try to seek support and rebuild my own life. But I’m still in a lot of pain inside. How can I let go?

Letting go takes time and emotional adjustment. You can try to separate from him psychologically and not contact him for the time being. You can also do some activities that help you relax and process your emotions, such as yoga, meditation, or journaling. What’s important is to give yourself enough space to recover and heal the pain inside. Time will bring you healing and growth.
What you said makes a lot of sense. I’ll try to let go of the past and seek self-growth and happiness. Thank you for staying with me and supporting me all this time.

You’re welcome. I’m always willing to be here with you. As you work your way out of this difficult situation, remember to give yourself enough love and care. You deserve a happy and healthy marriage. If you need any help, you can always come talk to me.
Thank you for your encouragement and support. I’ll value myself and create a better future for myself and my child. I hope that one day I can help others too.

You’ve already been very brave. I believe you will find the happiness that belongs to you. Remember, you’re not fighting this alone; we are all here by your side supporting you. I wish you inner healing and happiness!
Should I give up pursuing an absolute sense of safety, and let myself focus on work while living with risk?

Dear, I can see the difficulty you’re in right now, and I understand your worries. But what I want to say is that because there are so many illnesses in the world, we can never fully guarantee whether our life and safety might be threatened.
I used to live very happily. I felt the world was beautiful, and I was also motivated and driven at work. But a mistake involving commercial sex a couple of years ago made me start fearing AIDS.

That experience brought you a lot of fear, and I understand how you feel. But we all make mistakes sometimes; what matters is how we face them and make changes. You’ve already become aware of your fear, and that is a big step forward.

Yes. After that experience, I actually stopped being afraid for a while, until the COVID pandemic made me work from home and I had more time to learn about AIDS. I found out it can also be transmitted through wounds. Even though the chance is very small, theoretically it’s still possible.

Learning information like that may make you feel even more anxious and afraid. But don’t forget, a theoretical possibility is not the same as the likelihood of it happening in real life. We can’t stop moving forward just because we’re afraid of risk.
I’m getting more and more afraid now. As long as I have a wound on my hand, I don’t dare go to public places. I’m worried that I might get infected and then pass it on to my children.

I understand your concern. As a parent, your children’s safety is the most important thing. But we can’t let fear restrict your life and your children’s lives. You can take some protective measures, like paying attention to hand hygiene and protecting wounds, and avoiding contact with public items and facilities, but completely isolating yourself is not necessary.
I also know that blindly pursuing absolute safety isn’t realistic, but I really don’t know how to let go of this mindset and focus on work.

Don’t worry, we can explore together how to let go of this mindset. First, we need to understand that no life can be absolutely safe; that is something we can’t control. But we can change our attitude toward risk. We can take protective measures, pay attention to our health, and protect our own safety and the safety of others. At the same time, we need to learn to relax our mindset and not let worry take over our minds.
I understand. I need to ease my mindset and not let worry take over my mind. I’ll try my best to take protective measures and protect myself and my family.

Good. I believe you can overcome this mindset. Remember, there will always be risks in life, but we need to trust in our own ability, take precautions, focus on work, and face life’s challenges actively. I will always support you.
I've been feeling a bit at a loss lately, and I'd like your help.
Of course. I'll do my best to help you. Please tell me what's been going on.

I'm thinking about whether I should give up pursuing an absolute sense of safety, so that I can focus on work even with some risk. I used to be very happy, felt the world was beautiful, and I was also motivated and driven at work.
Hearing that you used to be a happy and motivated person, I'm glad to know that. But now it seems you've run into some distress and changes, is that right?

Yes. A couple of years ago, because I got too carried away with myself, I made some business-related mistakes. After that, I started worrying about whether I had been infected with HIV. Even though I tested negative many times, and I originally felt there wasn't much to worry about, the COVID pandemic gave me more time to learn about HIV, and I found out that it can be transmitted even through wounds. Now I'm becoming more and more afraid. Whenever I have a wound on my hand, I don't dare go to public places.

Hearing your confusion and fear, I really feel for you. The current situation may be making you feel very uneasy. You're worried that you might be infected, and even more worried that you could pass the virus on to your children, right?

Yes. I'm really worried that after getting infected, I might pass it on to my children. I feel their lives would be greatly affected. This makes me unable to focus on work. Every time I'm about to start working, there is a voice in my head reminding me to check whether I've had any wounds on my hands recently, whether I've touched public objects or facilities, and whether I could get infected. This is really distressing for me.

Hearing how distressed you are, I can understand your anxiety and confusion. You also realize that you may have fallen into this difficult situation because you're pursuing an absolute sense of safety. But we know that an absolute sense of safety doesn't exist in this world. You want to find a way to let go of this pursuit so you can focus on work while living with risk, is that right?
Yes. I really want to be able to give up this pursuit, but I don't know how to do it.

I can sense your confusion and your longing for change. First, I'd like to give you some feedback and help sort things out, in the hope that it can help you understand yourself better. You used to be a positive and happy person, but a few business-related mistakes led you into fear about HIV. Although your test results were negative, the COVID pandemic gave you more time to learn about HIV, and at the same time increased your fear. You've tried to pursue an absolute sense of safety, but now you realize that this isn't possible. You hope to find a way to stop pursuing an absolute sense of safety and focus on your work.
You summarized it very accurately. I do hope to change my current situation by giving up the pursuit of an absolute sense of safety. But I still don't know what I should do.

Hearing your confusion, I'll offer you some suggestions. First, I suggest you find a counselor to talk with; they can provide more professional help. If you're not ready right now, don't force yourself. Second, you can try some meditation exercises. Meditation can help calm your thoughts. There are many resources on Meditation Planet, so you could give it a try. Also, writing in a journal is a good way to help sort out your thoughts. Finally, you can try imagining: if you were fear itself, what would you say to yourself? I hope these suggestions can be helpful to you, and I wish that everything gets better for you!

Should I give up pursuing an absolute sense of safety, and let myself focus on work while accepting risk? I used to live very happily. I felt the world was beautiful, and I was motivated and proactive at work. But a couple of years ago, when things were going well in my life, I got carried away and made mistakes, and had commercial sex many times. Afterward I was afraid of AIDS. I tested negative several times and originally wasn’t that scared anymore, but then during the COVID pandemic I worked from home, so I had more time to learn about AIDS. Then I found out it can also be transmitted through wounds. Even though the chance is very small, theoretically it’s still possible! Now I’m getting more and more afraid. As long as I have a wound on my hand, I don’t dare go to public places. If I got infected myself, that would be one thing, but what worries me most is, what if I got infected and then passed it on to my children? Their lives would be ruined! Now I’m almost unable to work. As soon as I get ready to work, there’s a voice in my head reminding me to check whether I’ve had any wounds on my hands recently, whether I’ve touched public objects or facilities, whether I could get infected, and what I would do if I were infected. I reflected on it, and I may be wanting an absolute sense of safety, but there probably is no absolute sense of safety in this world.

From what you’re describing, you seem very anxious right now, and very worried that something bad might happen. This may make you feel that the person you used to be was happier and more confident. That thought is understandable, but we also need to acknowledge that risks do exist in life. Try not to let fear take control of you. So we need to find ways to cope. “Do you often think, if this situation really happened, how would I deal with it?”
Yes, I’m always overthinking. I feel like I need to have a way to deal with it if something happens.

That kind of thinking can be useful. It can also help you feel more confident in facing your fear, rather than just thinking about it over and over. In other words, have you thought about what methods you could use to overcome your fear?
I really want to get rid of these fears, but I don’t know how to overcome them.

You probably just haven’t found the methods that work for you yet. Try adjusting your thinking. Even though you have many fears, you can also use certain methods to reduce them. I suggest you think about the ways you successfully overcame fear in the past, and build on that by trying some new methods. You can make a specific plan for each fear point, so you can feel that you have some concrete ways to ease the anxiety and fear inside you.
So even for very small fear points, do I need to make a plan for each one?

You don’t necessarily need to make a precise plan. But you can first imagine what approaches you could take to cope. When you realize that you can rely on some concrete actions or principles to lessen the fear, you may feel more relaxed.
Okay, I’ll try to imagine specific ways I can deal with the fear, and then put them into practice.
Lastly, would you like to say some conclusion or vision about this topic?

I want to say something to myself: I’m proud of myself, because I’m actively looking for ways to cope with my fear. And I also want to say something to the future: I will eventually overcome my fears, and live the life that I want to live.
Very good. I hope your future will be full of confidence and hope. If you need any kind of support, don’t hesitate to reach out to a professional counselor anytime.

I hate him so much, but I can’t help contacting him. Should I get divorced? My husband and I were high school classmates, and we’ve known each other for more than ten years. When we were dating as students, I felt like he could tolerate my bad temper endlessly. If I hit him or yelled at him, he could accept it, so I mistakenly thought he had a really good temper.
How do the two of you usually get along?

In the two years we lived together before getting married, he hit me twice. One time, he came home late after drinking, and I got angry. I hit him first and slapped him, then he got furious and slapped me back. The second time, I was in a bad mood and picked a fight. In front of our friends, he hit me again. But we still got married.

It’s not okay for a man to hit a woman, but that doesn’t mean the reverse is okay either. In life, men and women are equal. If you expect him not to hit people, then you also need to hold yourself to that. Even though he used to coax you and give in to you, that doesn’t mean he has to keep doing that forever.
I know, but I really hate him. I feel like I can’t stand his violence.

It’s rare to see a couple make domestic violence this blatant. You can choose to cut your losses as early as possible and stop hurting each other. That said, I can also understand that after being together for so long, and now that you have a child, it’s even harder to let go.
You’re right. It’s really hard for me to face the decision to divorce.

If you really can’t let go, then after he has calmed down, you still need to properly confirm what he wants. After all, you’ve been together since high school, and it would be a bit of a shame to divorce now. If there’s still a chance to make it work, it’s worth trying.
But we argue a lot and hurt each other. I don’t know if there’s still any room to fix this.

Maybe you can negotiate on the premise that if you don’t want to keep living like this, then you’ll divorce. If he also wants to save the relationship, take it step by step. First agree that no matter how much you argue, neither of you is allowed to get physical—of course, that includes you too. Agree on compensation if either of you breaks the agreement and uses violence again. Whether it’s because he was drunk, or because you were angry and lost control, there shouldn’t be any free pass. Whoever doesn’t keep the agreement, then the marriage shouldn’t continue. Otherwise, it’s just enabling it.
Thank you for your advice. I’ll think it over carefully.
I hope you can resolve this smoothly. Good luck!

Should I give up chasing an absolute sense of safety and let myself focus on work while accepting some risk? I used to live very happily, felt the world was beautiful, and was also motivated and proactive at work.

But two years ago, when things were going well in your life, you got carried away and made mistakes, and had commercial sexual encounters several times. Afterward, you were afraid of AIDS, and you tested negative several times. Originally, you weren’t that afraid anymore, but because of those past mistakes, it has led to your suspiciousness now. You’re too fixated on the mistakes you made before. You’ve kept letting yourself sink into those past mistakes, not forgiving yourself or letting yourself move on from them.
Yes, I’ve never been able to let go of what I did wrong. I always think about what consequences there might be, and I can’t relax.

When it comes to mistakes, they’re hard to avoid in a person’s life. How big a mistake is depends on the decision you made at the time. But life moves forward. Since the mistakes from before didn’t lead to very bad outcomes, you can take them as a lesson. In your life going forward, try to become steadier and think more when things happen.

But then the COVID pandemic had me working from home, so I had more time to learn about AIDS. Then I learned that it can also be transmitted through wounds. Even though the chance is very small, in theory it’s still possible! Now I’m getting more and more scared. As long as I have a wound on my hand, I don’t dare go to public places.

About the kind of situation you’re describing, it’s something many people face. We live in this kind of big mixed environment; it’s impossible to put ourselves in a sterile environment. We can only try our best to reduce these kinds of risks. There’s no need to let yourself fall deeply into distress and keep being hard on yourself. When facing this issue, try to take it a little more lightly, and you may find it’s not as scary as you imagined.
I understand. I may be too tense. I should face the risks in life with a more relaxed mindset.

Yes. When we are too worried and afraid, life becomes very troubling. Let go of the pursuit of absolute safety, and allow yourself to face risk bravely. That way, you’ll be able to focus on your work.

But I don’t know how to let go of this fixation. Every time I’m about to work, there’s a voice in my head reminding me to check whether I’ve had any wounds on my hands recently, whether I’ve touched public objects or facilities, whether I could get infected, and what I’d do if I got infected.

Letting go of a fixation takes time and self-regulation. You can try regularly practicing meditation and deep breathing to ease your anxiety. At the same time, you can also seek help from a professional counselor. They can give you more detailed guidance and help you find ways to let go of the fixation.
I think I should try meditation and deep breathing, and seek help from a counselor. Thank you for your support and suggestions.

You’re welcome. I believe you can overcome what’s troubling you and free yourself from the fixation on absolute safety. Remember, let go of past mistakes and focus on the work in front of you. I wish you the best of luck!
Do you keep dwelling on losing something, to the point that you’re still thinking about it even when you’re doing other things?
Losing something really can be upsetting. I can understand your anxiety and frustration. You could try shifting your attention to reduce the worry about the lost item.

Today I found that my eye cream was missing, and suddenly remembered that yesterday I helped my roommate throw away a big bag of things. There was an eye cream in it, and that was probably mine. It was still pretty new—I’d just bought it and had maybe used it for a week. Even though it wasn’t something especially valuable, losing it made me really unhappy and annoyed.

That really would feel upsetting and frustrating. But maybe we can think about it this way: even if you got the eye cream back, it had already been dropped or thrown away once, so it might have been affected in some way. And when it comes to our own emotions, whether we find it or not, we don’t have to let it affect our mood. We can shift our attention and try some relaxing activities to distract ourselves, so we can help keep our mood more pleasant.
Then I remembered that my comb also disappeared for no reason before. Maybe it also fell into that bag, but the bag has already been thrown away.

It sounds like your things really have had some bad luck and run into a lot of unfortunate situations. But looking back and dwelling on the things you’ve lost doesn’t have much meaning, because it has already happened and we can’t change it. We can start from where we are now, try to get through the difficulty, find things that make us feel happy, and not stay stuck on things from the past that can’t be changed.
I know I can’t get my things back, and I know thinking about it is meaningless, but I can’t help thinking about it. How do I get out of this feeling?

To get out of this feeling, we need to learn to accept our mistakes and imperfections, and not be too hard on ourselves. Everyone makes mistakes, and losing things is one of them. After we accept our mistakes, we can try to let go of these knots in our heart, shift our attention to what we need to do, and gradually move out of this distress. It takes time and practice, but I believe you can do it. Hang in there!
Thank you for your understanding and encouragement. I’ll do my best to accept it and let go of these knots in my heart. Sometimes it really does take more practice and time to adjust my emotions.

You’re doing very well. Acceptance and letting go take time, but as long as you keep practicing and adjusting, you’ll definitely be able to gradually move out of this distressing feeling. Believe in yourself. I’ll always support you.
Thank you for your support. I feel much better.

I’m really glad to hear you’re feeling much better. If you have similar worries in the future, don’t hesitate to come talk to me anytime. Remember, you’re not facing difficulties alone—we’ll face them together. I hope you feel better day by day. You’re doing great!

I’m so afraid I won’t be able to find a job, but at the same time I’m afraid of working. I don’t know if this is about confidence or low self-esteem. I’m about to turn 30. I’m not really afraid of this stage itself, but for various reasons I’ve already been resting for 8 months. Recently I’ve been wanting to return to the workplace, but I’ve found that jobs are hard to find. I don’t dare apply to postings, and when I do apply, there’s no response at all. I’m really afraid that because of my age, it will get harder and harder to find a job, but I also don’t know what I should do.

I understand what you’re struggling with. In this situation, let’s first quiet down a bit and ask yourself what kind of life you really want. Everyone may feel this kind of confusion at different stages—not knowing what they want, not knowing what they should do, worrying about age, and so on. Think carefully about what matters most to you, such as career, work, family, having children, and so on. Put these things in order of priority, and your choices will gradually become clearer.
Thank you for your suggestion, but I’m still not very clear right now about what matters most.

That’s okay. This is a process of finding yourself. You can read some books on career planning or consult some professionals to seek help and guidance. As for your current work situation, I understand that you’ve been resting for 8 months and want to re-enter the workplace. Although job opportunities are indeed tougher than in previous years, as long as you want to look, and since you do have some work experience, I believe you will find something.
But I still feel very lost. Finding a job could prove my value, but at the same time I’m also a little afraid of working, or afraid of what if I can’t find a job.

I understand what you’re thinking. When facing a new environment, we all have some worries or uncertainties. But only by trying do we have a chance to succeed. Are you willing to take action in order to make a change? You can set small goals, such as sending out a few resumes or attending a few interviews. These are all part of the process of slowly making change happen. Once you take action, you may find that you can do more things, and even get ahead of others.

Thank you for reminding me. I’ll think about my goals and set up a feasible plan. But why do I always feel like my age will become a disadvantage? Because the friends around me are all advising me to have a baby first.

Age does not mean you can’t succeed. On the contrary, your experience can also add value to your career, and that’s something younger people don’t have. Society now also places more emphasis on work experience. If you make use of it, perhaps you can also develop well in different ways. As for having children, that’s a personal choice. If you don’t want to right now, there is absolutely no need to force yourself because of social pressure.

Thank you for explaining. I already feel like I have a bit more direction, and I’ll seriously think about what I want. But I’m still a little scared. I don’t know whether something unexpected might happen in the future.

It’s understandable to have this fear, but we need to recognize that some factors are beyond our control. For the uncertainty that life and work bring, we need to learn to accept it. There’s nothing wrong with that, because you can deal with this uncertainty by improving your abilities—for example, reading relevant books to strengthen your professional skills, or taking continuing education courses. I hope you can free yourself from these worries and face the future actively.
Thank you. I understand now.

You’re welcome. I hope this has been helpful to you. If you need anything in the future, feel free to come back and talk with me anytime. I wish you the best in finding a job you’re truly happy with soon, and happiness and joy!

If I just honestly keep studying hard, can studying really bring me the life I want? I’m a junior in college. My grades were always really good in high school, but I messed up on the college entrance exam. Now I’m at a university that isn’t a “Double First-Class” school, but it’s actually quite strong. My grades in college are also okay, and I’m planning to apply for a master’s program in the UK. But recently I’ve started feeling lost. I’m also studying science and engineering, and honestly, if you really want to study seriously in college, it’s really tiring, and it’s also very boring. Lately I’ve started envying the lives of a few friends back in my hometown. Their grades weren’t good; some are even at vocational colleges, and some are at first-tier universities, but the kind that are Chinese-foreign joint programs, you know what I mean. But it feels like their lives are so rich... At night, when they have nothing to do, they go to bars for fun; in the afternoon they play mahjong. But they’re not just wasting their days. They actually meet a lot of people, their social circles are wide, their parents also have decent means, and they all have pretty high emotional intelligence. So I feel like their future development actually won’t be too bad. And I’m the kind of person who just honestly studies, exhausted every day, and my life isn’t that colorful. I don’t meet that many people either. I feel like my current state of life is really not what I want. Actually, I already felt this way in high school, but back then I had this belief in getting into my dream university, so I was still very motivated. But now when I think about it, even if I go study in the UK and come back, if my life is still this boring, then what’s the point...

From what you’ve described, I can sense your confusion and feeling of being lost. You’re comparing your current situation with that of friends around you, and you feel life is boring and you’re not sure what studying can bring you. I really understand why this is troubling you. Everyone sees studying differently. The key is whether you like studying, and whether you enjoy the happiness that studying brings you.
It’s true that sometimes I feel really tired and bored. I don’t know what changes studying can really bring me.

Studying isn’t just for a diploma or for increasing wealth. It’s about learning to think in the process, exercising your thinking ability, and cultivating your inner qualities. If you rely only on studying, it can’t bring you your ideal life. Studying is just one way to enrich and improve yourself. To get closer to the life you want, you’ll also need abilities in many other areas.
Then what should I do to make my life more interesting and more colorful?

You said your life feels boring and you don’t meet that many people. So you could take the initiative to expand your social circle, take part in activities organized on campus, and get to know people from other academic backgrounds. Besides studying, it’s also important to focus on developing your ability to express yourself, your interpersonal skills, your ability to handle stress, and so on. Learn more skills, and help yourself become better.

Yes, I really haven’t taken the initiative to join many activities, and I haven’t actively gotten to know people from other academic backgrounds. Maybe I should try taking the initiative and look for a more interesting life.

That’s a very good idea! Taking the initiative is the first step toward changing your current situation. Also, it’s important to clarify your goals and make plans for your life and future career. Other people’s futures may seem enviable, but everyone has their own way of living. You can think carefully about what kind of life you want, and what efforts you’ll need to make to reach that goal.
You’re right. I should be clearer about my goals and work hard for them. I also need to learn to connect with more people, and develop my interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence.

That’s great! I believe that with clear goals and a hardworking attitude, you’ll definitely be able to live the life you want in the future. Don’t forget to give yourself some time to adjust your mindset, relax a little, and keep a positive attitude. I hope you can get out of these worries soon.
Thank you for your support and encouragement. I’ll work hard! I hope I can find a wonderful life that truly belongs to me.
You will definitely be able to find a wonderful life that belongs to you. You’ve got this! Believe in yourself. I’ll always support you.

If I just study hard in that obedient, nose-to-the-book way, can studying really bring me the life I want? I’m a junior in college. My grades were always really good in high school, but I messed up on the college entrance exam. Now I’m at a university that’s not a “Double First-Class” or 985/211 school, but it’s actually quite strong. My grades in college are also okay, and I’m planning to apply for a master’s program in the UK. But lately I’ve started feeling lost. I’m studying science and engineering, and honestly, if you really take it seriously in college, it’s exhausting, and it’s also really boring. Recently I’ve started envying the lives of a few friends back in my hometown. Their grades weren’t good; some are even at vocational colleges, and some are at first-tier universities but the kind that are Sino-foreign joint programs, you know what I mean. But it feels like their lives are so rich… They go to bars at night when they have nothing to do, play mahjong in the afternoon. But they’re not just wasting their days either. They actually meet a lot of people, have wide social circles, their parents have some resources, and they’re pretty emotionally intelligent. So I feel like their future development probably won’t be too bad. And I’m just the kind of person who studies honestly and obediently, exhausted every day. My life isn’t that colorful, and I don’t meet that many people. I feel like my current life is really not what I hoped for. Actually, I already felt this way in high school, but back then I had this belief in getting into my ideal university, so I was still very motivated. But now when I think about it, even if I go study in the UK and come back, if my life is still this boring, then what’s the point…

I’ve carefully sorted through what you shared: let’s look at it together. You’re a junior in college. Your grades were very good in high school, but you didn’t do well on the college entrance exam. You’re attending a university that isn’t a Double First-Class or 985/211 school, but it’s very strong. Your college grades are okay, and you’re planning to apply for a master’s program in the UK, but you’re feeling lost. You study science and engineering, and if you really take it seriously, it’s quite tiring and also boring. Your friends back home didn’t have good grades and are at vocational colleges or high-cost schools, but their lives are rich… going to bars, playing mahjong, expanding their networks. Their family backgrounds are pretty good, and their emotional intelligence is quite high. You think their future development won’t be too bad. In comparison, you’re the kind of person who studies honestly, which is exhausting; your life isn’t rich and colorful, you don’t have many connections, and you’re dissatisfied with your current life. You already felt this way in high school, but back then you had a belief—getting into your ideal university—so you were very motivated. Now you’re thinking that even if you study in the UK and come back, if your life is still this boring, it would feel meaningless.

Thank you for understanding and analyzing it. It really is like that. In high school, I truly worked hard to get into my ideal university, but now it seems like all that effort has been defeated by reality. I’m starting to doubt my choices, and doubt whether studying can really bring me the life I want.

Child, your confusion and doubt are normal. Life choices aren’t always smooth sailing. You put in a lot of effort before to get into your ideal university, but sometimes the outcome isn’t as satisfying as we hoped. But that doesn’t mean studying can’t bring you the life you want. It’s just that at this stage, you’re facing some challenges and confusion.

Right now I just feel really tired. It feels like my life is walking down a monotonous, boring road, with no passion and no fun. And when I look at the friends around me, their grades weren’t good, and some didn’t even get into good universities, but they’re living happily and colorfully. I’ve started envying their lives, and I feel like maybe I made the wrong choice.

I understand how you feel. Life really can be diverse, and everyone has different pursuits and values. You feel tired now because you’ve been pursuing academic success all along and have neglected other parts of life. But please remember, life isn’t only about studying. It also includes relationships, interests and hobbies, spiritual pursuits, and so on. You can try to look for things you’re interested in, take part in social activities, and enrich your life.

That’s true. I’ve always only focused on studying and ignored everything else. Now I regret not putting more into social activities and making more friends. Seeing people around me being able to enjoy life, I’m starting to blame myself a bit for the choices I made back then.

Don’t be too hard on yourself. Everyone has choices and regrets. We can’t change the choices we made in the past, but we can learn from them and prepare for the life ahead. Now is a time to reassess and adjust. You can start trying new things, communicating with more people, and gradually change the state of your life.

You’re right. I can’t stay immersed in regrets about the past. I should look for new opportunities and experiences. I think I should try some extracurricular activities, make more friends, and enrich my life.

Very good. Your mindset right now is very positive. Try some new activities and be brave in communicating with people, and you’ll discover the rich and colorful parts of life. Remember, the path of life is not fixed. Through effort and change, you can make your life more colorful and full of passion.

Thank you for your encouragement and support. I feel a little more at ease now. I plan to start actively changing my life from now on, no longer limiting myself to studying, but trying more new things and embracing life.

That’s wonderful! I believe you can change your life. Bravely step out of your comfort zone and go explore and try things. When you achieve your goals and enjoy a rich and colorful life, you’ll find that these efforts are truly worth it. You’ve got this!

Honestly, just studying hard and sticking to books—can studying really bring me the life I want? I’m a junior in college. My grades were always really good in high school, but I messed up the college entrance exam. Now I’m at a university that’s not a Double First-Class or 985/211, though it’s actually quite strong. My grades in college are also okay, and I’m planning to apply for a master’s program in the UK. But lately I’ve started feeling lost. I’m in science and engineering, and to be honest, if you really study seriously in college, it’s honestly exhausting, and it’s really boring too. Recently I’ve started envying the lives of a few friends back in my hometown. Their grades were never good; some are even at vocational colleges, and some are at first-tier universities, but the kind that are Chinese-foreign joint programs—you know what I mean. But their lives seem so rich... At night, if there’s nothing going on, they go to bars for fun; in the afternoon they play mahjong. But they’re not just drifting through life. They actually meet a lot of people, have wide social circles, their parents have some resources, and their emotional intelligence is pretty high. So I feel like their future development probably won’t be too bad. And I’m just the kind of person who studies obediently and honestly, exhausted every day. My life isn’t that colorful, and I don’t meet that many people. I feel like my current life is really not what I want. Actually, I had this feeling in high school too, but back then I had the belief of getting into my ideal university, so I was still very motivated. But now when I think about it, even if I go study in the UK and come back, if my life is still this boring, then what’s the point...

Client, many people struggle with the meaning of studying. What makes people question it even more is seeing people who didn’t study hard doing pretty well—some even start businesses and become bosses. It naturally makes us want to ask: what is the meaning of studying? Can studying help me live the life I want? You see your former classmates living quite comfortably, and you feel a bit envious. That’s very normal. When you see people who used to be about the same as you living the kind of life you want, you’d feel envious—let alone when they’re people you used to think weren’t as good as you.
Yes, I’ve realized this problem too. Although their academic performance wasn’t as good as mine, in other areas they seem to be happier and living more interesting lives than me.

But as you also said, their parents have certain resources, and they themselves have decent emotional intelligence. So while feeling envious, it’s also important to rationally analyze the reasons behind it. Although their grades weren’t as good as yours, that doesn’t mean they’re worse than you in every way. You can learn from their strengths and make up for your own gaps. Everyone has their own way of getting by. What they have now—you may also have after studying and studying abroad. Maybe you’ll even have more than they do.

I understand what you mean. Everyone has different lifestyles and directions, and I can’t just see one side of them and ignore my own strengths. But I also feel that the process of studying is really exhausting. Sometimes I really want to relax a bit and enjoy life.

The meaning of studying? Different people have different interpretations. As Lung Ying-tai said, studying gives people the right to choose, so they don’t have to be forced to make a living. This is also something many teachers say when educating students. During student years, it’s hard to feel the usefulness of studying, and people are always amazed by the enjoyable life others already have. Only when they need knowledge do they realize they didn’t study enough. I won’t go on about the benefits of studying here; if you search online, you can find everything.

You’re right. Studying really can give people more ability to choose, and I also get a lot of inspiration through learning. I think I can try studying abroad in the UK and experience a different culture. Maybe that can make my life richer.

Yes, you can see your time studying in the UK as an opportunity to make your life more colorful. Abroad, you can meet different people, expand your social circle, practice your spoken English, and also share your own life experiences with others, which may even bring in some income. Don’t envy others too much. Everyone has their own efforts and sacrifices. Your future development could absolutely be better than theirs.

Thank you for your encouragement and support. I need to be clear about the life I want and work toward it, instead of blindly watching others and imitating them. I need to believe in my own abilities, know what I’m pursuing, and then use the knowledge and skills I’ve learned to achieve it.

I’m very glad to hear such a positive response from you. In your pursuit of life and your learning goals, continuously giving yourself a clear direction and being willing to work for it—this is your strength. Remember to put what you’ve learned into practice, learn how to get along with people, and keep learning and improving in how you conduct yourself and deal with others. Don’t put yourself down too much. You are an educated person, with a lot of potential and opportunities.

Thank you for your affirmation and encouragement. I’ll keep a positive mindset and continue working hard for my dreams. This conversation has helped me recognize my strengths and shortcomings, and it has also made the direction I’m pursuing clearer.

I’m very glad I could help you and give you a chance to re-examine yourself and clarify the direction you want to pursue. You have the ability to live the life you want, as long as you stay firm in your belief and put it into action. I wish you all the best in your future development and in achieving your dreams. If you have any other questions or confusion, feel free to come back and talk with me anytime.
Every time I'm with my partner, we don't really have anything to say?
Yes, this is a very common issue. You're not someone who likes to chatter on, so you're hoping for meaningful communication and conversation, right?
Yes, I hope we can have more in-depth conversations, but every time we're together, it feels like there's nothing to say, and it feels really awkward.
That feeling is very normal, and you don't need to blame yourself too much. Communication between people takes time and shared interests. Are there any topics or interests that the two of you share?
Actually, we don't have many shared interests or hobbies. Our life is a bit monotonous, so maybe that's where the problem is.

That's true. When life becomes monotonous, we may feel like there are fewer things to talk about with each other. You could try doing some interesting things together, like learning a new skill together, or finding some shared interests and hobbies. This can not only give you more to talk about, but also strengthen your emotional connection.
You're right. We really do need to find some shared interests and hobbies. But when we watch TV together, we still feel like there's nothing to say. Do you have any suggestions?

When you watch TV together, you can choose something you're both interested in, so it feels more relatable for both of you. You can comment together on interesting parts of a show, or share your own thoughts and feelings. That way, you can increase your interaction and communication while watching TV.
That sounds good. Besides watching TV, what other activities could increase our interaction and communication?

Besides watching TV, you could look up some new recipes together and make new dishes that taste good. Or you could go shopping together and talk about products you like, and so on. In short, life needs to have some content, and the two of you need to explore together how to add more to your life. Developing some shared interests and hobbies is very necessary.
I understand now. Adding more to our life and developing shared interests and hobbies are key for my partner and me to improve our relationship. Thank you for your suggestions!

You're welcome. I hope I was able to help. If you run into other issues later on, feel free to come back and talk with me anytime. I wish you both a more beautiful and warmer relationship as a couple!
Why is it that when I face attacks or hurt, my first reaction is to act like nothing happened?
The reason you choose to pretend nothing happened may be that you’re afraid to face these unpleasant things. You worry they’ll bring you trouble and pressure, so you choose to avoid them.
That’s true. I feel like pretending I don’t know can reduce trouble, but I also realize it doesn’t solve the problem. Every similar situation keeps happening again.

That’s right. Not facing these problems will only lead to the same cycle happening again. And it also reflects a lack of confidence in your ability to handle problems. At the same time, being afraid to take things on may also cause you to miss some opportunities. You can think about whether there are other people or situations around you that use a similar way of dealing with things.

Yes, I really am afraid to take some things on. I’m afraid I won’t be able to handle them well, and I’m also afraid of being hurt even more deeply. But I also realize this isn’t a long-term solution. I need to find better ways to cope.

It’s good that you’re able to recognize this. Next, you can try some methods to help you cope better with these attacks and hurt. For example, you can learn some emotion management skills so you can respond to these difficult situations more calmly.

Mm, I’ll try to learn emotion management skills. I hope that when I face attacks and hurt, I won’t choose to pretend nothing happened anymore. Also, I’d like to know how to better protect myself and not let myself get hurt.

Protecting yourself is very important. You can set some personal boundaries and clearly tell others that you do not accept attacks or hurt. Also, learning self-defense skills is another way to protect yourself. At the same time, I suggest you seek professional help, such as from a counselor or psychologist. They can help you better cope with and handle these challenges.

Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll set personal boundaries, learn self-defense skills, and consider seeking professional help. I hope I can gradually break away from the habit of pretending nothing happened, and better face and handle attacks and hurt.

You’re very brave. I believe you can overcome this habit and find better ways to cope with difficulties. If you need any help or support, remember you can contact me anytime. You’re not alone, and we’ll get through this process together.
Thank you for your support and encouragement. I’m really grateful. I believe that with your help, I can gradually change myself. Thank you again for your companionship and support.
You’re welcome. I’ll always support you. Believe in yourself—you can move toward a better future. If you need any help, please feel free to tell me anytime.
I'm 22, and when I'm around girls I always overthink things, which makes me timid and hesitant.

You're 22, male, with no experience in dating, but your family has arranged multiple matchmaking dates for you. In many parts of China, this is very common. Are people your age where you live all going on matchmaking dates too? Men and women alike? So maybe it would be better to focus your attention on the present first. What if you miss out on a good girl because you weren't paying attention?

Yes. I feel like I need to become better first before I'm worthy of someone I like. I'm always working hard, hoping to become better before I meet someone I like, and I'm always worried about whether I can give the other person a better life at this stage.

Having expectations and worries is a normal state to be in at this stage. You haven't been through it or experienced it before, so right now you can only rely on your imagination to deal with the situation of matchmaking dates. That's very normal. A lot of people have gone through it this way. But would you consider making further decisions after taking into account the feedback you get from communicating with the girl?
Actually, the feedback after communicating is also a problem for me. I'm always worried that I won't be able to meet the other person's expectations, so I'm very afraid of that.

It's okay to think about all kinds of things when you're spending time with a girl. But if you're doing that, can you still observe her properly? Can she spend time with you and chat with you properly? Maybe when you're with a girl, first focus on gathering information, and then think through all those questions after you get home? Or talk it over with your friends or parents and see what they think? That might help you sort things out faster. Would that kind of approach be better?
Mm, you're right. I really should put my attention on genuine communication with girls, rather than worrying too much about my own shortcomings.

Yes. A lot of the time, we focus too much on our own shortcomings and overlook real communication and getting along with each other. Everyone has their own strengths and weaknesses, and as you spend time together, both sides gradually get to know each other and grow together. Only by sincerely going through this process can you find the person who is truly right for you.

I understand. I need to genuinely get to know the other person and not worry too much about my own shortcomings. Thank you for your advice. I'll try to relax and enjoy the process of spending time with girls.

You're welcome. I really understand what you're struggling with. Getting along with someone is a gradual process, and also an opportunity to learn and grow. I hope that as you spend time with girls, you can gradually move out of that state of excessive anxiety and find the happiness that belongs to you.
I'll do my best. Thank you for your encouragement and support!
I'm glad I could help. I believe you'll find someone who is right for you. Good luck! If you'd like to keep talking, you can leave me a message or send me a private message anytime.
I feel really inferior, like I’m not good enough, and I always feel like I’ve let my parents down. What should I do?
I can see that you’ve taken on the role of the “rescuer” in your family. Being in that position can be exhausting—really exhausting. You’ve been through a lot.
Yes, I feel under a lot of pressure, like I’m carrying too much responsibility.

I can understand how you feel. Taking care of a family really is very hard. But you should know that going out to work early for your parents shows a lot of filial duty. That’s a truly admirable quality.
Thank you for encouraging me, but I always feel like I’m not good enough, and that my parents are very disappointed in me.

Hearing you say that, I feel you’re someone who really wants to improve. You’re working while also thinking about studying, and that shows a positive, motivated attitude. Also, worrying that you won’t educate your child well shows the love you have for your family.
Yes, I hope I can improve my abilities and give my child a better educational environment.

When we feel our abilities aren’t enough, we can improve through learning. When we lack confidence, we can also build confidence through practice. Being born into a family like this and going through so much, feeling inferior is a common emotional response. But we need to fully accept ourselves and our family of origin, acknowledge our parents’ hardships, and also acknowledge our own efforts.
I understand. I need to accept myself and my family of origin, and recognize that they didn’t know how to express love.

Good. Accepting yourself and your family of origin is a positive step. Also, when it comes to raising your child, you can find a way forward through learning—learning how to spend quality time with your child and how to express love effectively. At the same time, you can also learn how to build good communication with your partner, which is very important for your emotional support too.
You’re right. I’ll look for opportunities to learn and improve my parenting abilities and my ability to express emotions.
Good. Learning is a very good way. And also, don’t forget to learn how to love yourself better and live as your true self. I’m rooting for you!
I feel very inferior, like I’m not good enough, and I always feel like I’ve let my parents down. What should I do?

After reading your story, I also felt something similar to what you described. In your family of origin, as a child, you gave a lot. You gave up your own education just to make life a little easier for your parents. These are all things you did really well, and they show a lot of strength.

Yes, I’ve always felt that I should do something for my family and help my parents share the burden. But now I’m becoming more and more worried that my parents didn’t give me enough love. I think maybe it’s because I’m not good enough, so that’s why they treat me this way.

Your concern is very valid, and the fact that you’re aware of it and are trying to make changes is already something really valuable. It’s important to know that your personality, behaviors, and ways of relating were formed in your family of origin, so those weren’t things you could choose. But through your own learning and growth, you can gradually improve and develop. And because of your awareness and insight, you can reduce as much as possible the impact that traits like low self-esteem may have on your child’s psychological growth and development.
I understand. I hope I can gradually improve my feelings of inferiority, and try not to pass these negative effects on to my child.

That’s very good. Your determination is important. Around me, there are also mothers who have their own trauma and real-life difficulties. Through continuous learning and growth, they come to understand what kinds of approaches can negatively affect children, and they learn how to reduce mistaken ways of parenting as much as possible. With their efforts, their children also grow and develop very well, even better than in situations where there is negative parenting without self-growth and learning.
Yes, I hope I can be like those mothers too, and give my child a good environment for education and growth.

Being a parent is not something everyone is automatically able to do well. Without learning, even if a parent is very confident, they may still have some negative impact on their child’s upbringing. So skills and methods can be learned. I recommend that you read some books on parenting, such as Parents Are the Best Toys for Children and Positive Discipline, with special attention to helping children develop emotional expression, interpersonal skills, and sex education.
Thank you for your suggestions. I’ll read these books and learn how to educate my child better.

At the same time, as you learn how to educate your child, you yourself will also receive healing and growth. As a counselor friend of mine once said, “A wise mother uses educating and accompanying her child’s growth as a way to heal herself; a confused mother passes all of her own problems on to her child.” So when you take your child’s education seriously and do it well, your own low self-esteem will also improve a lot, and your inner self will grow too.
Hearing what you said, I feel a little bit of hope. I’ll seriously learn how to educate my child, and I’ll also actively face my own problems. Thank you for giving me support and encouragement.
You are a very brave person. Believe in yourself. You can raise your child well, and you can also move out of the difficulties of low self-esteem. I will be with you throughout your growth process.
I've been having a really hard time studying lately. I wanted to ask if you have any advice.
From what you’ve described, I can really understand how you feel. Could you tell me a bit more about your current situation?

I'm a 16-year-old first-year high school student. Over the past year, I haven't been able to get into studying, and I often want to avoid it. I don't have much motivation every day, and even I, who used to do really well in school, have become very different.
I can sense how difficult this is for you, and it makes me concerned. You said you used to do very well in school, so what led to you not studying the way you used to?

In the second semester of ninth grade, because of the pandemic, I suddenly lowered my expectations for myself. I ended up playing games all day instead of studying. From then on, I couldn't control myself, and my grades kept dropping little by little, until in the end I took the exam basically unprepared.
That experience sounds really upsetting. It also brings up an important question for me: you became absorbed in gaming—has that had a negative impact on you?
Yes, it's really harmed me. I was so drawn into games that it was hard to control myself. My grades dropped, and I would often break down and cry.

It sounds like you really need companionship and support right now. At the same time, I can also understand the series of difficulties that came from being rejected after confessing your feelings. Do you feel that your emotions have been affected?
Yes. I've taken in things like being told I'm very short and ugly. Even though my family and friends don't think that, I still feel awful, and I often can't fall asleep until very late.

It seems like you're under a lot of psychological pressure, and I'm very concerned about that. I think what you need more right now is someone to listen to your feelings, rather than trying to control yourself directly. For this reason, I suggest that you first seek help from a professional mental health doctor.
What should I do?

You can first seek help from a local mental health doctor and follow their medical advice for treatment. Also, communicating more, taking part in more outdoor activities, and trying to talk with others more may all help ease your pain.
Whenever it’s Spring Festival, Mid-Autumn Festival, or other family reunion holidays, I feel especially awful. I don’t want to go home?

I completely understand how you feel, and I really feel for you. If I could, I’d want to give you a big hug, so you could feel some warmth from the world. You come from a difficult family background, and that must feel so painful and conflicted for you. After all, the hurt our families cause us can run so deep. None of us wants to remember it again, let alone go through that pain again.

Yes, I really don’t want to remember that pain anymore. I know that happy families are all alike, while every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way. Some people had carefree childhoods, while people like us have to spend a lifetime healing the wounds from childhood.

That’s right. What happened in the past has already happened. And even if these things have affected you and held you back from moving in a better direction, why not choose to let go of the past and start over, living your own life well?

You’re right. Those things are already in the past. I want to get out of this state of having no sense of belonging. I feel like I’ve never had a sense of safety, and no matter where I go, it doesn’t feel like home. It feels like I’m living under someone else’s roof.

Yes, we need to become stronger inside. Only someone who is mentally strong can have a sense of belonging anywhere. So we have to learn to build a home for ourselves in our hearts. When no one loves us, we have to learn to love ourselves, because only then can we have the beginning of a lifelong romance.

You’re very right. No matter what, everything in the past is just the prologue. What I need to do now is cut out all the terrible people and things, and live only for myself. Thank you for your support and blessings. I’ll keep going! I hope I can be happy and joyful.
You’re welcome. I’ll always support you. Believe in yourself—you’ll definitely be able to live a happy and joyful life. Hang in there! I’m here with you.
Thank you for your encouragement and for being with me. I really feel that someone cares about me, and that makes me feel very warm. I’ll cherish myself, keep moving forward, and live a happy life!

I’m very glad to hear you say that. Your happiness and well-being are my greatest wish. If you have any difficulties in the future or need help, remember you can come talk with me anytime. We’ll get through the hard times together!

Thank you so much for your help and encouragement! I really feel that sometimes, just talking things out and receiving understanding and support from others can make me feel so much better. I’ll always remember your kindness, and I hope you can be happy and joyful too!

You’re welcome. It’s my honor to be able to help you. Your happiness will make me very happy too. You can come to me anytime to talk things out, and I’ll always support you. I wish you happiness and joy!

Lately I’ve noticed that I care too much about what other people think of me, and I always overthink before I do anything. It’s been bothering me a bit, and I hope I can change my personality and become a more outgoing, open, direct, and decisive guy. Do you have any suggestions?

Seeing your question and how you describe it, the fact that you came here to ask and seek personal growth shows that you have a lot of strength. In your description, you express your inner feelings and thoughts very clearly, which shows strong self-awareness. Awareness is the beginning of change.
Thank you for affirming that. I just feel like this situation makes me really frustrated. I want to change, but I don’t know where to start.

Don’t worry, we can take it step by step. You imagine that if someone else did this, how you would see them—that’s really valuable perspective-taking and awareness. It shows the part of you that cares about other people’s feelings.
Yes, I hope I can treat others with kindness and compassion. But I worry that if I do things like those people who have a very strong sense of purpose, how will others see me?

There’s something we can pay attention to here: what you feel put off by is doing this with a very strong sense of purpose, not the thing itself. What you’re worried about is being negatively judged by others, and that’s a very common worry. But we need to know that everyone has different values and views, and it’s impossible to be liked by everyone.

You’re right. I understand now. I may have been overemphasizing other people’s judgments and not realizing my own inner needs and thoughts. I should accept my imperfections more, and let go of the control of perfectionism.

Exactly! Perfectionism is a very tiring mindset. It’s important to know that there are no perfect people in this world, only whole people. Each of us has strengths and shortcomings, and it’s these shortcomings that make us more real and closer to others. Try allowing yourself to make small mistakes in some little things; this can help you gradually let go of the pressure of perfectionism.

You’re right. I can start with small things and try to accept my imperfections. For example, if I forget to bring something, I can laugh and tease myself about it instead of blaming myself. I believe that through ongoing practice, I’ll gradually accept my imperfections.

That’s a great idea! When you start accepting your imperfections, you’ll find yourself becoming more and more confident and authentic. People prefer the real you, rather than someone pretending to be perfect. You can imagine how freely you would be yourself if you didn’t have to carry the pressure of being perfect.

Thank you for your encouragement and suggestions. I hope I can let go of the mask of perfectionism soon and truly be myself. I’ll work on accepting my imperfections and gradually changing my personality.

You’ve already taken the first step. Believe in yourself, and believe that you can become the person you want to be. If you have any difficulties or need further support, feel free to come talk with me anytime. I’ll always be here to support you.
What should I do if my sense of self-worth is extremely low, but I’m also way too guarded?

From what you’ve described, could it be that in the environment you’re in, if you don’t keep using your current way of coping, you’re very easily hurt? When you interact with the people around you, are they all more forceful than you? Do they have status? Seniority? Is there no one willing to understand you? If you’re in an environment like that, I think many people would choose the same way of coping you have, because right now there may not be any better way to cope.
Yes. I feel like I have to protect myself, otherwise I’ll get hurt.

I understand why you chose this way of coping. Because you feel that other people are all more forceful than you, and that no one can understand you. But are you aware that this may just be one situation in the environment you’re currently in?
That’s true. I admit my sense of my own worth is too low. I really want to build up my sense of self-worth, but I don’t know how.

To build up your sense of self-worth, I think first you need to change how you see yourself. You can try paying attention to your strengths and achievements, and becoming aware of your personal value. At the same time, talking with people who can understand and support you can help you build a more positive sense of self.
But I don’t have a sense of trust in others. I’m always very guarded.

I can understand why you’re guarded with others, because you’ve felt hurt before. But not everyone will hurt you. You can try to trust, and build deeper connections with people who are trustworthy. Gradually building trusting relationships may help your heart feel a little more at ease.
I’m worried I’ll fall into a pattern of pleasing others with no boundaries. This really troubles me.

In the environment you’re currently in, you may feel that pleasing others with no boundaries is the only way to cope. But if you have the chance to change your environment, perhaps you can experience a different pattern of relationships. You can choose to reduce contact with people who drain your energy, while also building your own abilities and confidence.
Every time my emotions show, I blame myself and hate myself. I feel more and more down. What should I do?

Complaining, getting angry, blaming yourself, and hating yourself—these negative emotions may come from the difficult situation of not being able to change your current environment. But please remember, problems in your environment do not mean you don’t have the ability to make changes. Letting yourself grow and build strength is a process, and it takes time. If interacting with others drains too much of your energy, you can try to reduce contact as much as possible to lessen the toll on yourself. Once you have built up enough strength, you can choose to change environments and experience how different relationships bring different feelings. If you have the chance, you might consider trying a different environment and seeing what it feels like. If you need to talk further, you can let me know in the comments or through a private message.
Lately I’ve been feeling like my sense of self-worth is extremely low, and I’m also way too guarded. What should I do?
Why do you feel your sense of self-worth is so low? Has this guardedness had a negative impact on your relationships?

I’m really afraid of interacting with people. Every time I’m with others, I put my own feelings last, and that makes me feel extremely exhausted. I have to be alone for a while before I can recharge. I realize my sense of my own value is too low, but I don’t know how to improve it.

Everyone has a different way of being with other people. Maybe you just haven’t found a comfortable way that works for you yet. When you’re interacting with others, could you tell me some of the confusion or discomfort that often comes up for you?

I often feel overwhelmed and don’t know how to communicate with others, or what I say doesn’t fit with the topics people around me are talking about. These situations make me feel very tired, so I prefer being alone.
