Sometimes in life we feel a sense of loss and dissatisfaction with our current situation, and those are very normal emotions. But avoidance isn't a way to solve problems. Maybe you could try making some small changes to spark motivation in your life, such as setting some new goals or finding some new interests. Remember, difficulties are only temporary, and you still have many chances to change your life.
In the past, when things were bad, I was always able to adjust myself, but now these negative feelings have been going on for more than a year and are still continuing.

Negative emotions that continue for more than a year can have some impact on mental health. I suggest you seek professional counseling or treatment. By talking with a professional, you can better process these negative emotions and find more positive ways to address them.
Thank you for your advice. I'll consider trying to seek professional help.

You're welcome. Seeking professional help can be very helpful. I hope you can regain your confidence and face life's challenges actively. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask me anytime. Good luck!
I was sexually assaulted when I was 5. I want to get better. Can you help me analyze and correct my thoughts?
I can sense the suppression, anxiety, conflict, and struggle inside you. If something like this happened to anyone, they would feel a lot of pressure, pain, and distress.
Yes. I’ve always felt a lot of self-blame and guilt.
That’s a very common reaction, but you need to know this was not your fault. You were an innocent child.
But I feel like I was an accomplice, because I didn’t refuse at the time, and I even nodded.
You were so young, and your understanding of these things was limited. And the other person was older than you. Instinctively, you felt that not resisting would be safer.
But even now I still feel very guilty. I feel like I didn’t protect myself well enough.
You need to know that when you realized there was danger, you were able to bravely resist and protect yourself. That is truly remarkable. At the very least, you stopped them from hurting you further.
But I feel like I didn’t do well enough, and I still let myself get hurt.
You already did your best. Don’t be too harsh on yourself. You are someone with courage and strength, and that cannot be denied no matter what.
I always feel so much pain now. I feel like I’m trapped in darkness.
The emotions you have been holding inside are very powerful. When you could no longer endure it, you chose to bravely resist. This also shows us your courage and strength.
But why do I still feel pain?

This may be because your idea of being “dirty” and your inner sense of morality are too strong. You need to try to accept what happened in the past, and accept the state and thoughts you had at that time.
How should I accept it?

First, accept that at the time you were young and didn’t understand, and you weren’t clear about the meaning or consequences of what was happening. Then, accept the effort you made to bravely resist, as well as the conflict and contradiction inside you. Most importantly, let go of the pain from the past and put your energy into your future life.
You’re right. I should let go of the past so I can live well in the present and the future.
Exactly. Letting go of the past is key to feeling light and free again. Believe in yourself. You have the ability to come out of this pain and start again.
Thank you for your support and encouragement. I’ll do my best to let go of the past and live better.
I’m very glad I could help you. Remember, you are not fighting this alone. We all support you. Hang in there!

Why have I developed fear and resistance toward work? When I think about going to work the next day, I feel negative. I don’t feel safe about work, and I feel like life is hopeless and unhappy. Please help me build the right motivation.

In just a few words, I can feel a lot of helplessness and fear. Although I don’t know what the reason is, your fear of work, and the feelings of not seeing hope and not being happy, really touched me. The fact that you can say, “Please help me build the right motivation,” tells me that you are, in yourself, positive, motivated, and someone who wants meaning in life. Since there is limited information, we can talk about it briefly. I have a few questions that may be helpful to you.
Okay, what questions do you have?
First, could you tell me about the background of how you got your current job? How did you get this opportunity? Why did you choose this job? What needs does this job meet for you?

I studied a related major before, and I’ve built up some experience in this field, so I got this job opportunity. I chose this job because it’s very helpful for my development, and it also meets my financial needs.

I understand. Next, I’d like to invite you to notice what meaning might be behind your fear of work. After you feel the fear, what do you feel? What methods might help reduce the fear? And after the fear is reduced, how would you evaluate this job?

I think my fear of work may come from not being confident in my abilities, and worrying that I won’t be able to handle the job. When I feel afraid, I feel uneasy and under a lot of pressure. I’m trying to improve my abilities by doing some work-related training, hoping that this can reduce the fear. If the fear can be reduced, I believe I would have a more positive view of this job.

Your awareness is very important. Understanding your inner feelings can help you cope with fear. Next, I’ll ask some questions about the environment. In your current work environment, what factors make you feel unsafe?

I feel that the competition in the work environment is very intense, and the interpersonal relationships are complicated. I’m worried that I won’t be able to fit into this environment or that I’ll be excluded. These factors make me feel unsafe.
I understand your concerns. So, how do you see the relationship between the work environment and the work itself?

I think the work environment directly affects my work state and performance. If the environment is good, I’ll be more engaged and proactive in handling my work. On the other hand, if the environment is not good, I may feel more confused and helpless.
I see. So, what do you think the relationship is between this job and the meaning of your life?

I hope my work can have a positive impact on my personal growth and development, and also allow me to make some contribution to society. I think only this kind of work can make me feel that life has meaning.
I understand what you’re pursuing. Next, I’d like to ask: what does your ideal meaning of life look like?
For me, the ideal meaning of life is being able to realize my own value, enjoy the sense of achievement that work brings, and share happy times with my family and friends.

Through our earlier conversation, I’m guessing you may have encountered some things or people that have interfered with how you’re experiencing life right now. These disturbances may be related to work or the environment. There are some things we cannot change, but we can accept them and heal through other ways. Life is not perfect, and it is not always happy. I hope you can live with your heart, get caught up in things a little less, and firmly believe that there is no obstacle you cannot get through. Hang in there! I hope things go your way soon. The sky is blue, you are here, and life can be beautiful. The world, and I, love you.
Thank you for your support and encouragement. I’ll do my best to adjust my mindset, believe that I can face the difficulties at work, and find joy in my work.

I’m very glad to hear your determination. I believe you can overcome the difficulties and find joy in your work. If you need to keep talking or have other questions, you can reach out to me anytime. I wish you all the best!

I keep trying to control myself so I don’t curse gods and Buddhas. Is this religious obsessive-compulsive disorder? How do you deal with it? I just can’t control myself from cursing gods and Buddhas. My family believes in Buddhism and burns incense every day. One time a thought flashed through my mind, wanting to curse gods and Buddhas, and after that I couldn’t control the urge to curse. I tried really hard to stop myself. Every day when I open my eyes I want to fight it, but I’m constantly controlling myself not to curse. Now I can control myself and not curse for a whole day, but inside I’m in so much pain, constantly resisting myself. Now when I see a cross, I associate it with Jesus and want to curse too. Because of this, I saw a counselor before. She said God’s thoughts are different from ours and that I won’t be punished, that if I curse then I curse, I can curse however I want. But I can’t do that. I’m afraid that if I go along with my obsessive-compulsive symptoms, I’ll get worse and worse. I also can’t get past this in my heart, just keep cursing like that. Now I’m thinking about this every moment, controlling myself. It’s been half a year since August until now... I control myself every day, and I’ve also read books on Morita therapy, about accepting things as they are and doing what needs to be done, but it’s still like this. Even when I’m doing things, I think of this all the time and try to control it. Are you saying I have to live with this pain for the rest of my life? Control myself every day? I really feel like I’m being tortured to death... It’s been half a year and it keeps going. I don’t want to die.

I can see you’re caught up in struggling with not being able to stop yourself from cursing gods and Buddhas. On one hand, you can’t help cursing; on the other hand, you feel it’s wrong and that you should control it.
Yes, I feel extremely conflicted and torn. I don’t know what to do.
This kind of conflict and feeling torn must be very painful for you, especially when it involves such a big topic as religious faith, which can make it even harder.
Yes, I really feel awful. Controlling myself every day so I don’t curse gods and Buddhas feels very painful.
I’m curious, what kinds of things do you usually curse about? Is it that they don’t really fit with the ideas of gods and Buddhas?
I don’t like the false feelings they bring me, and I feel that when I see a cross I’ll think of Jesus, and I’ll want to curse too.
I understand. How do you feel during the process of cursing? Is it relieving, or do you feel like you’ve found something?
Sometimes cursing makes me feel relieved, but sometimes I also feel pain inside, because I know it’s not right.
I understand how you feel. If you can try to feel what exactly is making you unhappy, and the inner reason you choose to curse, maybe we can start from there and make some adjustments.
I actually don’t know why I don’t like this behavior, but I’ve been trying my best to stop myself from doing it.
Sometimes we dislike a certain behavior because the consequences it brings us don’t feel good. Have you thought about what consequences cursing gods and Buddhas might bring you?
I’m worried that if I go along with my obsessive-compulsive symptoms, they’ll get worse and worse, and I won’t be able to pull myself out.

Actually, the things we worry about may very well not really happen. Maybe you could record the amount of time you spend cursing each day and how often it happens, to understand the real situation, and compare the data from when you don’t control it with when you do.
I think what you said makes sense. Maybe I can try recording it and see whether it really does get worse and worse.

Also, accepting yourself and the behavior of cursing gods and Buddhas may involve some different ways and attitudes. You can try giving this behavior a new meaning, seeing it as one of your traits or habits, rather than as torture and pain.
This perspective really could help me change my attitude. Thank you for your suggestion.
You’re welcome. I hope the suggestions above can be helpful to you. If you need, I can keep talking with you.

We have two children at home. The younger one is 1.5 years old, and recently he’s suddenly become especially clingy with me, his mom. Why is that? Dad and I both go to work every day, and the older child goes to kindergarten. Grandma stays home and takes care of the younger one.

Your baby is a year and a half old and has suddenly started clinging to you—when you’re at home, he wants you to hold him, otherwise he cries and fusses? Does he also cry and fuss when you leave for work?
Yes, that’s exactly it. I don’t understand why he keeps crying and fussing in front of me.
You’re also finding it hard to control your own emotions because of his crying and fussing, and you end up scolding him harshly. But even after scolding him, you still keep holding him.
Yes, every time I try to scold him, but I can’t control my emotions.
You’re not sure why he’s so clingy with you. First, let’s take a look at what’s typical for babies at this stage.
At a year and a half, a baby’s language development is still immature, so most of his needs are still expressed through crying.
By a year and a half, crying has already become more differentiated—crying because of hunger, cold, pain, tiredness, a toy being taken away, fear, being startled, and so on.
So, do you think he cries and fusses in front of me just because he wants me to hold him?
Or could there be some other need that you haven’t met?
When he cries and fusses in front of me, I first check whether he’s hungry, needs a diaper change, or is feeling lonely.
Starting from around six months, babies form a special emotional bond with their primary caregiver—their mother. They’re especially happy when they’re with Mom, and they cry and fuss when Mom leaves.
At this stage, babies may experience “separation anxiety.” When he can’t predict whether Mom will come back after leaving, he uses crying and fussing to resist the separation.
So, how should we respond?
As his mother, it’s important to know how to manage your own emotions, so your scolding doesn’t end up frightening the baby.

Mom needs to respond promptly to the child’s crying and fussing, and try to help him put his needs into words: “Are you crying because you don’t want to leave Mom?” “Was the toy you wanted to play with taken away?” As you respond to him, you can gradually help soothe his emotions.
I understand. From now on, I’ll try to calm myself down, understand his needs, and respond at the right time.

If the baby has separation anxiety, you can play games with him like, “Mommy is going to work—bye-bye, baby,” and “Mommy is back—baby is happy, right?” This helps him know that when Mom goes to work, she will come back, which can reduce his anxiety.
Okay, I’ll try playing these games with him and help him adapt better to being separated.
Very good. I believe your patience and understanding will help him get through this stage. He’ll gradually adapt to separation and cry and fuss less often.

My boyfriend used to have a messy life and loved to lie. I’ve become very controlling, and being with him feels so exhausting. We met through a matchmaking date. At first glance, I felt we weren’t a match, but later, as we slowly got to know each other, I got used to him. There’s a big gap between us in family background, education, and work. We’re two different kinds of people.

Dear girl, how are you? After reading what you wrote, I can feel your anxiety and pain. Ah, dear girl, a girl like a flower, meeting the wrong person really makes my heart ache for you. It also makes me angry.
His past makes me feel very uneasy. I’ve tried to control his behavior, but I’ve found myself getting more and more tired.
Dear girl, what you’re going through right now does sound really difficult. Are you trying to control his behavior because you have doubts about his past?
Yes. I feel that his past behavior was really bad, and it makes me unable to trust him.

I understand your worries and your sense of mistrust. But we can’t change his past; we can only decide how to handle our own emotions and the relationship. Have you thought about the shared interests and values between the two of you?
There’s a big gap between us in family background, education, work, and so on, and I’m worried this will cause problems.

Indeed, differences in family background, education, and work may bring some challenges to your relationship. But people who love each other can understand and support each other, and overcome difficulties together. Are you two able to grow and improve together?
I’ve tried to tolerate his past, but recently I found out he hid some bad behavior again.
Hearing that you found he had hidden some bad behavior again, I can understand your disappointment and confusion. Still, without a doubt, you and he need more communication and trust between you.
But I feel like he hasn’t shown any signs of changing. What should I do?

Dear girl, you’ve already become aware of the problem, and that is a very important step. Next, you can communicate with him properly and tell him about the confusion you’re feeling and what you need. Try giving him a chance and see whether he is willing to make changes for the sake of your relationship.
I’m not really sure whether he will truly change. I feel extremely tired, and I don’t know whether I should keep holding on to this relationship.

Dear girl, I completely understand your exhaustion and confusion. Before making a decision, may I ask if you’ve thought about your own bottom line and boundaries? Maybe you need to give yourself some time to calm down before making a decision. Remember, your happiness and health are very important.
I feel like it’s really hard for me to let go of him, because I’ve already given so much.

Dear girl, the things that have already happened can’t be changed. But you can control your choices in the future. Don’t let the “sunk costs” of the past tie you down in your pursuit of happiness. Even if it means breaking up, it would be for the sake of your own happiness and health.
I really don’t know what the right thing to do is.

Dear girl, everyone’s situation is different, and I can’t make the decision for you. But I can give you some suggestions. You could find a counselor and seek professional help, and explore together how to resolve the problems between you. At the same time, spend some time paying attention to your own needs and feelings, and don’t ignore your inner voice. You deserve to be loved and respected.
Thank you for your advice and support. I’ll think about it.
Dear girl, you are brave, and you will make the best decision. No matter what you choose, I support you. I hope you can find your true happiness and joy. Believe in yourself—you can do it!
How can he pull away so quickly? Is it being heartless, or being rational?
I’m sorry to hear what you’ve been through. As a guy, I’ve also done this kind of hurtful thing to an ex before.
We’re long-distance. Why would my boyfriend not reply to my messages from noon all the way through the whole night, and then the next day when I said I was sad and upset, he just acted helpless?

At the root of it, there must have been some problems in the way you two were getting along—like too much pressure in daily life, not being able to communicate well, and then things building up over a long time, leading to where things are today.
For the next two days after that, neither of us paid attention to the other, because this thing about replying to messages has happened many times before. It’s always like this.
My suggestion is to give each other some time to calm down, and then find a chance to talk things through calmly.

That night I posted on Moments about “letting go,” and then I found that he had deleted the QQ status where he said I would walk with him. I just hoped he would come and coax me a little on his own, but in the end he left even faster than I did.

A woman only has expectations of her man and loves him when she feels dissatisfied and anxious like this. But you also need to be clear that when things aren’t good between you, like right now, everything you do may make him feel annoyed, and it will be hard for him to feel your love.
Then I posted another Moment where I was crying my eyes out, with his favorite photo of us together, saying it was the final goodbye. He still didn’t contact me on his own.
The state you two are in right now really isn’t good, but the way you express your emotions may make him feel a lot of pressure. Men often feel at a loss when facing a woman’s emotions.
Why is it that when I say I cried, he doesn’t feel sorry for me? He still hasn’t contacted me. Can he really stay that calm?
It may be that he doesn’t know how to face your emotions. Some guys choose to avoid things when facing their girlfriend’s emotions. I hope you can have a deeper conversation with him.

It’s not like I’m insisting on anything. Even if we’re separating, am I not even worth him taking a little time to say one sentence? Just because I said I wanted to let go, does he think there’s nothing between us anymore?
He may not really understand your true thoughts and feelings. Communication is a very important part of this. You can try to talk with him honestly and let him understand what you need inside.
So whatever I do, whether I’m happy or sad, it has nothing to do with him anymore? How can he pull away so quickly? Does he not have any feelings at all?
A relationship needs both people to work together to maintain it. Maybe it’s not that he has no feelings at all, but that right now he may not have the capacity to give you more love and care.
Even if it were just an ordinary friend, if they found out the other person was crying, they would politely comfort them a little, right?
We all hope to receive care and understanding, but sometimes people’s emotional responses are not exactly the same. Maybe he just hasn’t expressed it in the right way.
Last time we were also on the verge of breaking up because of this. He didn’t contact me for five days, and in the end I was the one who contacted him first, and we barely kept it going.

It’s inevitable that there will be all kinds of issues and adjustments when getting along. You can try communicating in a more active and proactive way, or understand each other’s confusion and needs with a more open and accepting attitude. I hope things get better for you two.
I don’t have good relationships with anyone, there’s no emotional connection. I feel like I’m not even human?
Have you been feeling down lately? What makes you feel that your relationships with everyone are bad?
Nothing happened, but it also feels like something did happen. My relationships with everyone are bad. Even with my baby, who’s only a few months old, I don’t know how to communicate.

It sounds like you’re also feeling confused about communicating with your baby. Babies are indeed still very young, and the way they communicate is different from adults. We can improve communication skills with babies through learning.
I don’t have emotional communication with my parents, and it’s the same with friends and family. I don’t understand gratitude.

Gratitude is indeed important, but sometimes we may not really know how to express it. We can explore together how to express gratitude to family and friends. Maybe that can make the relationships more harmonious.
I stayed at my uncle’s home for half a year before, and now I basically never go there, and I never thanked them either.

You could reach out and express your thanks. Maybe the relationship between you can be rekindled. At the same time, you can also think about why there’s this sense of distance, and use conversation to clear up the confusion.
My little cousin is over ten years old now, and I don’t communicate with him either. Let alone other things. At work, I don’t interact with my coworkers.

Having a poor relationship with coworkers can create some difficulties at work. We can explore together how to improve your relationships with coworkers, such as improving communication skills or taking the initiative to participate in team activities.
When I finally manage to chat with someone, it can turn very unpleasant. Even just a few sentences can’t be pleasant.

Sometimes interpersonal interactions really aren’t easy. You can learn some effective communication skills, such as listening to the other person’s views and respecting their feelings. This may help avoid unpleasant conversations.
At home, I also communicate very little with my husband. When I see him, I feel like things are hard again.

Communication between spouses is also very important. You could try to find a chance to sit down with your husband and honestly express your feelings and confusion, and look for ways to solve the problems together. Communication can help you understand each other better.
Sometimes I feel like I have no drive. I don’t read.
People’s emotions and states go up and down, and motivation for learning can fluctuate too. We can explore together how to rekindle your interest and motivation for learning.

I talk very little with my mother-in-law and father-in-law, basically not at all. At work, a coworker who just graduated is my leader, several years younger than me, and earns more than a thousand more than I do.

These situations can all have a certain impact on a person psychologically. We can think together about how to improve your relationship with your mother-in-law and father-in-law, and also how to face challenges at work while continuing to develop your professional abilities. After all, difficulties at work can be overcome.

From when I was in school until now, I’ve been struggling with my mind. I went through a long, dark time. I thought I had come out of it, but later I found maybe I’d fallen back in again. When I meet setbacks, I feel very discouraged. There are too many problems, and nothing is easy.

I really understand the pain brought by the psychological struggle and dark times you’ve been through. What’s important is that you have already come out of it once, which shows that you have the courage and ability to overcome difficulties again. We can work together to develop some positive psychological coping strategies to help you handle setbacks and solve problems.
I feel like I’m good for nothing. I don’t study.

This kind of thinking is a common negative self-evaluation. We can work together to identify some of your strengths and achievements, and encourage you to try new ways of learning. Everyone has their own value and potential; sometimes it just needs to be reexamined and rediscovered.

You may have a little bit of postpartum depression, perhaps. Along with the pressures of life and work and the difficulties in interpersonal relationships, it has left you physically and mentally exhausted, feeling low, anxious, and worried. Your current situation actually isn’t very good and needs adjustment.
Thank you for your understanding and suggestions. I’ll try to improve my situation.

I suggest you first read two books by Zhang Defen, Meeting the Unknown Self and We Will Eventually Meet Love and Loneliness, and then find a professional counselor for some psychological support. That would be better. Wishing you well!
Okay, I’ll try reading these books. Thank you again for your suggestions and support.
You’re welcome. I hope you can get out of this difficult place soon and regain happiness and confidence. If you need anything, feel free to come to me anytime to talk.
Thank you very much for your encouragement and support. I really need this kind of help.
Don’t forget, you are strong, and you have the ability to overcome difficulties. Believe in your own strength. I’ll always be here to support you!
